content: Do not take ramipril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking ramipril, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication can harm the fetus. Ramipril is prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either alone or in combination with other medications. It is also used to reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in patients at risk for these conditions and to improve survival in patients with heart failure following a heart attack. Ramipril belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by decreasing certain chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more smoothly and enabling the heart to pump blood more efficiently. Ramipril is available as an oral capsule and is typically taken once or twice daily, with or without food. To help you remember to take it, try to take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take ramipril exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole, or you may open the capsule and sprinkle its contents on a small amount of applesauce (about 4 oz.) or mix it with 4 oz. of water or apple juice. Consume the entire mixture. This mixture can be prepared in advance and stored for up to 24 hours at room temperature or 48 hours in the refrigerator. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Ramipril helps control high blood pressure and heart failure but does not cure these conditions. Continue taking ramipril even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking ramipril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ramipril or any other ACE inhibitors, such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, or trandolapril. Also, inform them about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention aspirin, NSAIDs (e.g., indomethacin), diuretics, lithium, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart, liver, or kidney disease; lupus; scleroderma; diabetes; or angioedema (a condition causing difficulty swallowing or breathing and painful swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs). Let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking ramipril. Be aware that diarrhea, vomiting, inadequate fluid intake, or excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing lightheadedness or fainting. Consult your doctor before using salt substitutes containing potassium. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ramipril may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: headache, dizziness, cough, upset stomach, vomiting, excessive tiredness, or weakness. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; yellowing of the skin or eyes; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; lightheadedness; or fainting. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store ramipril in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include lightheadedness and fainting. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your blood pressure should be checked regularly to monitor your response to ramipril. Your doctor may order lab tests to evaluate your body’s response to the medication. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
